summary: A letter to TIP users from BBN about a revised TIP User's Guide in loose-leaf form. It lists new commands, including binary input and output, linefeed handling, wild device settings, and magnetic tape commands that apply to TIPs with the tape option. The letter explains the changes.

plainLanguage.summary: This letter tells TIP users about a revised user's guide and new commands. It also explains buffer limits, planned echo changes and where to report problems.

questions: what is a tip on the arpanet
subtitle: A BBN letter on TIP commands, buffers, echoing and user support.

tldr.problem: TIP users needed an updated guide and information about new commands, program changes and device-buffer limits.
tldr.mechanism: The letter lists commands, explains planned echo behavior and buffer allocation, and tells users how to report problems and suggestions.
tldr.outcome: A TIP system with the commands had been operating since late June, and BBN planned further guide updates and notices through NEWS.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 365 as Unknown and records no RFC that updates or obsoletes it. The letter describes planned and ongoing changes as of July 1972.

sections.title: New Commands and TIP Updates
sections.content:
The revised TIP User's Guide will use a loose-leaf format, add descriptions of new commands and include an alphabetical command list. The announced commands cover binary input and output, device settings, linefeeds, sending commands, wild sockets and magnetic tape operations.

The MAG commands apply only to TIPs with the magnetic tape option. A TIP system with these commands had been operating since late June. The RFC lists eleven TIPs in the network and says one would soon be installed at CCA.
sections.plainLanguage: The guide adds commands for binary data, device handling and magnetic tape. Tape commands apply only where that option is available.

sections.title: Status, Support and Buffers
sections.content:
New TIP software is loaded when a TIP is not in use. BBN plans to include a version number or a NEWS notice in the login greeting; users can request the news with @NEWS. The letter directs TIP problems to BBN's Network Control Center.

About 2500 characters of buffers are available for 63 devices, with one input and two output buffers per device. The RFC lists nominal buffer sizes by device-number range and says faster devices need larger buffers. BBN is considering more core memory or removing unused features at some sites.
sections.plainLanguage: Each connected device shares a limited amount of buffer space, and faster devices need more of it. BBN asks users to report TIP problems to its Network Control Center.

sections.title: Echo Command Changes
sections.content:
BBN plans to remove ECHO ALL, ECHO HALFDUPLEX and ECHO NONE, change the meanings of ECHO REMOTE and ECHO LOCAL, and add PHYSICAL HALFDUPLEX and PHYSICAL FULLDUPLEX. The RFC describes how the TIP will react to TELNET ECHO and NO ECHO characters depending on its physical and virtual modes.

The letter also reports that @@ is still often echoed incorrectly and calls that behavior a bug to be fixed.
sections.plainLanguage: The letter describes a revised set of commands for controlling where typed characters are echoed. It also acknowledges an echoing bug that was not yet fixed.

sections.title: Planned Work and User Suggestions
sections.content:
Planned changes include replacing PROTOCOL TO LOGIN with LOGIN using a Host number. Work in progress includes returning captured devices after hangup, output to high-speed devices, modem and tape improvements, and investigating reports of lost allocations.

Possible future work includes lowercase input for Model 33 Teletypes and a way for users to check TIP or device status. BBN says changes will be announced by NEWS and invites suggestions.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN lists work it is doing and features it may consider. It asks users to report problems and suggest improvements.
